900100.title: The Myth of Your Morning
900100.body:
The daily rite, mythologized: your morning as epic.

Every morning is a myth in miniature: the alarm is the call to adventure, the coffee is the elixir, the commute is the road of trials.

The personal mythologist maps the hero's journey onto the routine — the snooze button as the refusal of the call, the shower as the purification rite, the front door as the threshold.

The practice's power is reframing: the mundane becomes meaningful when the pattern is named, and the day begins as a story worth telling.
900100.summary: The daily rite, mythologized: your morning as epic.
key_points: Map the hero's journey onto routine.
Name the pattern; reframe the mundane.
The threshold is the front door.
The day begins as a story.

demo.title: Guided reading demo — The Myth of Your Morning

900101.title: The Legend of the Long Commute
900101.body:
The road of trials, daily: the commute as quest.

The long commute is the quest we didn't choose: the traffic is the monster, the podcast is the mentor, the arrival is the boon.

The legend grows with the telling — the construction detour becomes the labyrinth, the fellow commuters become the fellowship, the shortcut discovered becomes the secret path.

The legend's gift is the reframe: the lost hours become the journey, and the journey was the point all along.
900101.summary: The road of trials, daily: the commute as quest.
key_points: Traffic is the monster; podcast the mentor.

demo.title: Guided reading demo — The Legend of the Long Commute

900102.title: The Parable of the Inbox
900102.body:
Two hundred unread: the inbox as moral tale.

The inbox is the parable of the modern age: two hundred unread messages, each a small demand, together an overwhelming tide.

The parable's characters are the archetypes — the urgent that wasn't, the important buried, the newsletter that never ends — and the moral is the triage.

The parable teaches the letting go: the delete key as absolution, the unsubscribe as liberation, the empty inbox as nirvana glimpsed.
900102.summary: Two hundred unread: the inbox as moral tale.
key_points: The tide of two hundred demands.

demo.title: Guided reading demo — The Parable of the Inbox

900103.title: The Myth of the First Apartment
900103.body:
The tiny kingdom: founding myths of home.

The first apartment is the founding myth of adult life: the tiny kingdom with the leaky faucet and the magnificent view.

The myth's episodes are the trials — the furniture carried up five flights, the first meal cooked on two burners, the neighbor who became family.

The myth endures because it's the origin story: every later home is measured against the first, and the first always wins on meaning.
900103.summary: The tiny kingdom: founding myths of home.

demo.title: Guided reading demo — The Myth of the First Apartment

900104.title: The Tale of the Lost Keys
900104.body:
The small disaster, the great search: keys as quest object.

The lost keys are the quest object of domestic myth: the small disaster that reorganizes the whole morning.

The tale's structure is the search — the usual places, the impossible places, the place they were all along — and the revelation is always the obvious.

The tale's moral is the ritual: the hook by the door, the bowl, the habit that prevents the epic. The myth exists to teach the hook.
900104.summary: The small disaster, the great search: keys as quest object.
key_points: The quest object of domestic life.

demo.title: Guided reading demo — The Tale of the Lost Keys

900105.title: The Epic of the Deadline
900105.body:
The dragon with a date: the deadline as monster.

The deadline is the dragon with a date: it sleeps for weeks, then wakes hungry, and the hero must face it.

The epic's cantos are the phases — the denial, the panic, the flow, the all-nighter — each with its trials and its small victories.

The epic's wisdom is the pacing: the hero who starts early slays the dragon small; the hero who waits faces it grown. The deadline is undefeated, but it can be met.
900105.summary: The dragon with a date: the deadline as monster.

demo.title: Guided reading demo — The Epic of the Deadline

900106.title: The Myth of the Group Chat
900106.body:
The council of the pocket: the chat as pantheon.

The group chat is the pantheon in the pocket: the gods of the friend group, bickering and blessing in the small hours.

The myth's dramatis personae are the archetypes — the planner, the ghost, the meme-lord, the voice of reason — each playing their eternal role.

The myth's theology is the notification: the ping as prayer, the reply-all as ritual, the muted thread as exile. The chat is the agora; the phone is the temple.
900106.summary: The council of the pocket: the chat as pantheon.

demo.title: Guided reading demo — The Myth of the Group Chat

900107.title: The Fable of the Houseplant
900107.body:
The green dependent: the plant as moral teacher.

The houseplant is the fable's teacher: the green dependent that thrives on attention and forgives neglect, up to a point.

The fable's plot is the care cycle — the enthusiastic purchase, the slow forgetting, the dramatic rescue, the propagation of the survivor.

The fable's moral is the attention: the plant asks little and teaches much, and the watered plant is the watered life. The fable ends with the cutting shared.
900107.summary: The green dependent: the plant as moral teacher.

demo.title: Guided reading demo — The Fable of the Houseplant

900108.title: The Legend of Sunday Evening
900108.body:
The week's hinge: Sunday evening as threshold.

Sunday evening is the week's hinge: the threshold between the freedom of the weekend and the structure of the week.

The legend's mood is the bittersweet — the laundry, the lunch prep, the early night — each a small rite of the return.

The legend's wisdom is the ritual: the Sunday evening done well — the plan made, the bag packed, the rest taken — turns the hinge without the dread. The week begins at the threshold.
900108.summary: The week's hinge: Sunday evening as threshold.
key_points: Rites of return: laundry, prep, rest.

demo.title: Guided reading demo — The Legend of Sunday Evening

900109.title: The Personal Canon
900109.body:
The capstone: assembling your mythology.

The personal canon is the capstone: the collected myths of a life, assembled and bound.

The assembly's method is the gathering — the morning myth, the commute legend, the inbox parable — each recorded, each honored.

The canon's purpose is the continuity: the stories make the self coherent, and the coherent self can face the unstoried future. The canon is never finished; it grows with the life. The mythologist is the author; the life is the epic.
